recipes.name: Mixamo (Adobe) — royalty-free auto-rig + animation library
recipes.claim: Mixamo provides a free web service with royalty-free walk/run/idle/attack/death clips usable in commercial games without attribution or royalties, but you may NOT redistribute raw FBX files standalone, may not train ML on assets, and the fixed humanoid skeleton mis-fits the studio's exotic non-human species.
recipes.summary: Web service that auto-rigs an uploaded humanoid mesh and applies pre-authored motion-capture animations exported as FBX. Fastest path to a moving humanoid character: upload mesh, pick clip, export, retarget in Godot/UE5. Coverage spans locomotion, combat, social, and death cycles. Strong for human-proportioned roster members; severely limited for the studio's exotic species (animal-headed, scaled, shelled, avian) because the single fixed humanoid skeleton cannot accommodate non-standard proportions or extra limbs. Adobe operates the service; terms can change without notice.
recipes.design_implication: Use Mixamo to seed motion for human-proportioned cast members and as greybox reference for combat timing. Export to FBX, retarget in Godot 4 via UniRig or manually, then polish with Cascadeur. Do not make Mixamo load-bearing for the exotic species roster — those require bespoke rigs and authored motion. Treat Adobe-dependency as a strategic risk; archive exported FBX locally immediately after download.
recipes.license: Free service; royalty-free for personal, commercial, and non-profit use; no attribution required; no raw-file redistribution; no ML training on assets
recipes.commercial_notes: Royalty-free for commercial/personal/non-profit with no revenue cap and no attribution. Hard limits: (1) cannot distribute raw character or animation FBX files standalone — must be baked/embedded in a shipped project; (2) cannot create asset packs or blueprints that redistribute the raw files; (3) cannot train ML models on the assets. Adobe-operated service — terms are subject to change and the service could be discontinued; the 'at the time you use it' clause means past downloads remain covered under terms at point of use.

failures.symptom: Fixed humanoid skeleton mis-fits exotic species (animal-headed, scaled, shelled, avian)
failures.cause: Auto-rig assumes bilateral humanoid proportions; no spine variant or extra-limb support
failures.remediation: Restrict Mixamo to the human-proportioned cast; author bespoke rigs for exotic species

failures.cause: Adobe EULA explicitly forbids standalone distribution of character and animation files
failures.remediation: Always bake/embed into the shipped game project; never include raw FBX in open-source repos or asset packs

sources.claim: Content available for unlimited commercial or non-commercial use royalty-free; prohibited uses include distributing raw files standalone, creating asset packs that redistribute files, and training ML models on the assets.

recipes.name: Reallusion ActorCore — per-clip commercial mocap library
recipes.applicable_to: locomotion, combat, social, death (humanoid; some creature packs available)
recipes.claim: ActorCore offers 4,500+ royalty-free motion-capture clips purchasable per-clip or via subscription, licensed for commercial games including FBX/USD export to Unreal/Unity/Blender/Godot, but you may not redistribute the raw clips to third parties and may not use them for ML training.
recipes.summary: Reallusion's professional mocap marketplace with clips covering combat, locomotion, social, and specialty categories. Standard License is per-clip, royalty-free, perpetual after purchase, and covers commercial games and AR/VR. Export to FBX or USD with engine-specific presets for Unreal, Unity, Blender, and iClone. Clips are authored for humanoid skeletons (typically compatible with UE4/UE5 mannequin or iClone rigs); non-humanoid creatures are sparsely covered. The prohibition on redistribution to third parties means clips cannot be included in open-source engine plugins or asset store packs.
recipes.design_implication: Good source for high-quality combat and locomotion clips to drive the Spine rig-to-sprite pipeline. Buy per-clip for the specific actions needed (walk, run, attack variants, death) rather than subscribing speculatively. Retarget exported FBX to the studio's custom rigs in Godot 4. Budget for per-clip costs in the production spreadsheet — humanoid cast is well-served, exotic species are not.
recipes.license: Royalty-free, non-exclusive, worldwide, perpetual commercial license per clip; Standard License covers games and AR/VR
recipes.commercial_notes: Standard License explicitly covers commercial games, AR/VR, and interactive services. Royalty-free after purchase — no ongoing payments. Hard limits: (1) cannot redistribute or sublicense raw clips to third parties; (2) cannot use for ML/AI training; (3) cannot resell or distribute through stock libraries or competing markets. Physical 2D reproduction capped at 500,000 units. Perpetual per-clip model means shipping a game does not require an active subscription.

failures.cause: Library is humanoid-centric; non-human skeletons are a small minority of available clips
failures.remediation: Use for human cast; author or capture bespoke motion for exotic species

recipes.name: Rokoko Motion Library — subscription-gated humanoid mocap
recipes.applicable_to: locomotion, social, athletic (humanoid; no creature coverage)
recipes.claim: Rokoko Motion Library provides tens of thousands of humanoid mocap clips accessible via all subscription tiers (including free tier), explicitly licensed for commercial game use on export, but access appears subscription-tied and redistribution of raw assets is prohibited.
recipes.summary: Cloud-based marketplace of motion-capture clips embedded in Rokoko Studio; also available as a Unity Editor plugin. All five subscription tiers (Starter/free through Enterprise) include Motion Library access. The product page explicitly states assets can be used in commercial projects. Coverage is humanoid and performance-focused: locomotion, athletics, dance, combat. No exotic-species or creature coverage. The subscription-tied access model introduces a risk: it is unclear from public terms whether downloaded/exported clips retain a perpetual license after subscription lapses — verify with Rokoko before making it load-bearing.
recipes.design_implication: Useful for high-volume humanoid reference and secondary-character motion at low per-clip cost. Verify subscription-lock vs perpetual-export rights before relying on it for shipped clips — if exported animations are subscription-locked, cancellation could create a licensing gap mid-production. Not suitable for the exotic species roster.
recipes.license: Subscription-inclusive commercial license; exact perpetual-vs-subscription-locked status not confirmed in public terms
recipes.commercial_notes: Rokoko's product page explicitly says Motion Library assets can be used 'in any of your projects, including commercial ones.' However: (1) access is listed as a per-tier subscription feature, raising uncertainty about whether exported clips remain licensed post-cancellation; (2) the EULA prohibits redistribution and resale of raw assets; (3) Rokoko's general terms prohibit de-compilation, reverse engineering, and resale of software assets. Recommend confirming perpetual-export clause with Rokoko sales before treating as a long-term commercial source. No creature/exotic-species content.

failures.symptom: Licensing continuity unclear if subscription lapses
failures.cause: Motion Library access is presented as a subscription tier feature; perpetual-export clause not confirmed in public terms
failures.remediation: Contact Rokoko to confirm exported clips carry perpetual license; get written confirmation before shipping

failures.cause: Library is exclusively human motion capture
failures.remediation: Not applicable for the studio's exotic roster

recipes.name: Fab (Epic) marketplace — mocap animation packs (Standard License)
recipes.applicable_to: locomotion, combat, idle, death (humanoid; creature packs available per-seller)
recipes.claim: Fab's Standard License grants royalty-free perpetual commercial use of purchased mocap packs in shipped games; revenue-tiered pricing (Personal <$100k, Professional >$100k) covers the license; raw-asset redistribution is prohibited by the Standard License, and sellers may apply NoAI tags blocking ML training.
recipes.summary: Epic's unified content marketplace (successor to Unreal Marketplace and Sketchfab Store) hosts thousands of mocap and hand-keyed animation packs under the Fab Standard License. The Standard License is royalty-free and perpetual — a single purchase covers all commercial use in shipped products. Revenue tiers set the purchase price (Personal under $100k gross revenue, Professional over $100k) but do not restrict commercial shipping. Humanoid coverage is deep; creature/exotic packs exist but vary by seller quality. Tightly integrated with Unreal Engine 5 via direct import.
recipes.design_implication: Primary source for UE5-ready mocap packs — Standard License is clean for commercial shipping with no ongoing payments. Vet each seller for skeleton compatibility (UE4/UE5 mannequin vs custom) before purchasing. MoCap Online's free sampler pack on Fab is a zero-cost greybox starting point. Exotic-species clips exist but require manual vetting — check skeleton bind poses carefully for non-humanoid content.
recipes.license: Fab Standard License — royalty-free, perpetual commercial use; Personal tier for <$100k gross revenue; Professional tier for >$100k gross revenue
recipes.commercial_notes: Standard License explicitly covers commercial games — royalty-free, perpetual, no revenue-sharing after purchase. Revenue tiers (Personal/Professional) only determine purchase price, not shipping rights. Hard limits: (1) cannot redistribute raw purchased assets to third parties; (2) NoAI meta tag (seller-applied) blocks use for generative AI data collection. Important: the free Unreal Engine content granted under UE EULA (e.g. Quixel content) has separate terms tied to UE licensing — confirm those separately if mixing Fab Standard with UE-EULA assets.

recipes.name: MoCap Online — Unity/Unreal game-ready mocap packs
recipes.claim: MoCap Online sells per-pack royalty-free mocap animations with a Standard License covering commercial projects up to 1M end users and $1M revenue; no AI use permitted under any tier; raw file redistribution prohibited; larger projects need a per-project Commercial License.
recipes.summary: Professional game-focused mocap library with packs organized by genre (Mobility, Shooter, Fighter, Sports) sold on their own site and the Unity Asset Store. Every purchase includes a Standard License covering personal and commercial projects up to 1 million end users or $1 million revenue, royalty-free and perpetual. A per-project Commercial License covers up to $30M revenue with a certificate of rights. Animation quality is high and clips are pre-organized into locomotion sets, combat cycles, and death animations — directly useful for the Spine rig-to-sprite pipeline. AI processing (training, retargeting, synthesis) is explicitly prohibited under all tiers.
recipes.design_implication: Strong candidate for the human-proportioned cast's combat and locomotion cycles — the genre-specific packs map well to a JRPG action vocabulary. Purchase the Mobility + Combat packs for a complete walking/running/attacking/dying set. Verify the project will not exceed the $1M revenue threshold before launch or budget the per-project Commercial License. Strictly humanoid; exotic species are not covered.
recipes.license: Standard License: royalty-free perpetual, up to 1M users or $1M revenue; Commercial License: per-project, up to $30M revenue
recipes.commercial_notes: Standard License (included with purchase): commercial projects up to 1M end users and $1M revenue, royalty-free, perpetual, no attribution. Commercial License (per project, purchased separately): up to $30M revenue, 20-year protection, includes certificate of rights; sequels and new seasons each need a separate license. Hard limits across all tiers: (1) no AI use — training, retargeting, synthesis, or any AI-related processing requires a separate paid AI Usage Permit; (2) cannot resell or redistribute raw animation files; modified animations must be integrated into a completed project. Self-reporting required as projects approach thresholds; violations carry $10,000 penalty plus damages.

failures.cause: License explicitly prohibits AI-based animation processing including retargeting via AI models
failures.remediation: Use manual retargeting in Godot 4 / Blender; purchase separate AI Usage Permit if wave-1 AI motion tools will process these clips

recipes.name: Cascadeur (Nekki) — AI-assisted keyframe animation tool with commercial output
recipes.applicable_to: locomotion, combat, physics-driven action, creature (any skeleton the artist builds)
recipes.claim: Cascadeur is an AI-assisted keyframe animation tool (not a motion library) whose Pro/Teams tier ($396+/year) grants unlimited commercial use of exported FBX/GLB/USD animations in shipped games; the Free tier is strictly non-commercial; the Indie tier caps commercial use at <$100k revenue per year.
recipes.summary: Standalone animation software using physics-based auto-posing and AI interpolation to help artists create and polish keyframed animations — it is a production tool, not a pre-built clip library. The studio authors motion FROM SCRATCH or imports reference/BVH and refines it inside Cascadeur. All skeleton types are supported (humanoid, quadruped, exotic) because the artist builds the rig. Pro tier ($396/year) allows unlimited commercial use and perpetual license conversion after 12 months of annual subscription. Free tier: CASC export only, no commercial use. Indie tier: full export formats but commercial use capped at $100k/year revenue.
recipes.design_implication: Cascadeur is the polish stage of the motion pipeline — import mocap BVH from any source, clean and exaggerate timing, add secondary physics, export FBX to Godot/UE5. This is the tool that makes exotic-species motion viable: because the artist authors the rig, there is no 'humanoid skeleton mis-fit' problem. Budget Pro tier ($396/year); the perpetual license conversion after 12 months means one annual payment survives subscription lapse for the last released version.
recipes.license: Free: non-commercial, CASC export only; Indie: commercial <$100k/yr, full export; Pro/Teams: unlimited commercial, full export, perpetual after 12 months annual
recipes.commercial_notes: Pro tier ($396/year or $49/month): unlimited commercial use, all export formats (FBX, DAE, USD, GLTF), converts to perpetual license after 12 months of annual subscription. Indie tier ($96/year): full export formats but commercial use restricted to projects generating <$100k/year in aggregate gross revenue — this threshold will almost certainly be exceeded upon a Steam launch. Free tier: non-commercial, CASC export only. Cascadeur is a tool, not a content library — the license governs use of the SOFTWARE and its output, not pre-made clips; exported animations you author are your own IP.

recipes.name: Truebones — creature & animal mocap library (Zoo pack + Motherlode)
recipes.applicable_to: creature locomotion, animal combat, quadruped/biped hybrid motion
recipes.claim: Truebones sells FBX/BVH creature and animal mocap packs (75+ animals in the Zoo pack, 20,000+ clips in the Motherlode) with a stated 100% royalty-free commercial license via Gumroad, making them the only broadly available creature-mocap source; however, Truebones has a documented controversy around content sourcing authenticity that the studio must verify before shipping.
recipes.summary: Truebones (sold via Gumroad) is one of the only dedicated sources for creature and animal motion capture in FBX/BVH format. The Zoo pack covers 75+ species; the ProBones/Motherlode collections span 10,000–20,000+ clips covering quadrupeds, bipeds, and exotic movement patterns directly relevant to the studio's non-humanoid roster. Compatible with Unity Mecanim, Unreal Engine, Blender, Maya, and iClone. The royalty-free commercial license claim appears on the product page, but the license text is not a formal legal document — it is a product description on Gumroad. A separate site (truebones.net) documents community controversy regarding whether some Truebones content was repackaged from other libraries without proper licensing; this has not been resolved publicly.
recipes.design_implication: The most accessible creature-motion starting point for the exotic-species roster — animal locomotion patterns, quadruped movement, and multi-limb body mechanics can seed retargeting and Cascadeur refinement. CRITICAL RISK: verify provenance of specific clips before including in a shipped commercial title. Request Truebones' chain-of-title documentation for any clip intended for production use. If provenance cannot be confirmed, treat as greybox reference only and author final clips independently.
recipes.license: Stated 100% royalty-free commercial license on Gumroad product page; no formal legal agreement document publicly available
recipes.commercial_notes: Truebones' Gumroad product pages state '100% royalty-free license' and describe use 'in animated movie productions' and game engines (Unity Mecanim, Unreal Engine). FBX motions are described as compatible with commercial game workflows. Hard caveats: (1) no formal license agreement document — the 'license' is a product description, not a signed legal instrument; (2) documented community controversy exists at truebones.net regarding whether some content was repackaged from third-party libraries without proper authorization; (3) if any clips originated from a library with incompatible terms (e.g. academic/non-commercial mocap datasets), the royalty-free claim would not transfer. Recommend: use only as greybox/reference for production; commission or capture final shipping clips independently, or obtain written chain-of-title from Truebones.

recipes.name: Move.ai — video-to-mocap cloud service (markerless, commercial output)
recipes.applicable_to: locomotion, combat, performance capture (humanoid performers only)
recipes.claim: Move.ai processes smartphone or multi-camera video footage into retargetable skeletal animation (FBX/BVH/USD) via cloud AI; paid plans grant commercial use of exported animations; pricing starts at ~$15/month; output targets humanoid performers and cannot directly capture non-human creature motion.
recipes.summary: Cloud-based markerless mocap service: record a performer with a smartphone or consumer camera, upload to Move.ai, receive FBX/BVH/USD animation data. Quality has improved to production-usable reference level as of 2025. API integration allows embedding the pipeline into custom tools. Commercial use is granted on paid plans. Key constraint for this studio: motion is captured from a HUMAN PERFORMER, so the skeleton is humanoid — non-human species motion must be manually authored or retargeted with heavy cleanup afterward. Move.ai's core tech was partially acquired by Autodesk in 2026; service continuity risk exists.
recipes.design_implication: Use Move.ai to capture bespoke combat and locomotion performances for the human-proportioned cast at far lower cost than a studio mocap session. The studio director can self-perform rough motion for greybox and clean up in Cascadeur. For exotic species, capture a performer performing the INTENT of the movement (quadruped walk, claw attack) and heavily retarget/reanimate — this is reference only, not a clean source. Monitor service continuity given Autodesk acquisition of core tech.
recipes.license: SaaS subscription; commercial use of exported animations granted on paid plans
recipes.commercial_notes: Paid plans explicitly grant commercial rights to exported animation output (FBX, BVH, USD, BLEND). Non-commercial uses (education, research, personal projects) are covered by free/lower tiers. Commercial use definition includes business use, client work, monetized content, and professional production. Pricing from ~$15/month; enterprise/multi-person plans are custom-quoted. Caveat: Autodesk acquired core Move.ai technology in April 2026 — service terms and continuity may change under Autodesk ownership. Exported animations you generate are your own IP (you own the motion data derived from your performance).

failures.remediation: Use as performance reference and heavy-retarget in Cascadeur for exotic species; expect 80%+ manual rework

recipes.name: On-demand mocap studio session (Vicon/OptiTrack — commercial work-for-hire)
recipes.applicable_to: locomotion, combat, creature (puppeteered), custom performances — unlimited if the performer can do it
recipes.claim: Hiring a professional mocap studio (Vicon or OptiTrack marker-based) gives the cleanest, lowest-cleanup motion data with full commercial rights via work-for-hire agreement, but costs $1,000–$10,000+ per day and still delivers a humanoid skeleton — exotic species require puppeteering or actor-reference workflows.
recipes.summary: Traditional marker-based mocap studios (Vicon, OptiTrack) offer per-day rental or full-service sessions that produce BVH/FBX data with professional-grade accuracy. The work-for-hire contract transfers all IP to the commissioning studio — full commercial rights, no attribution, no redistribution limits. Suitable for high-priority animation cycles (hero combat, signature abilities) where quality justifies cost. Exotic species are handled by having actors perform the intended movement while the team maps it to non-humanoid skeletons in post — still a humanoid capture.
recipes.design_implication: Reserve for hero-character signature animations where quality is the deciding factor and no library clip meets the brief. Budget 1–2 days per major character's full animation set. For the exotic roster, brief the actors on body-mechanics intent (how a crab-humanoid hybrid would throw a punch) and do heavy retargeting in Cascadeur afterward. A 1-human studio will find this expensive relative to the pipeline's AI-augmented alternatives — treat as premium option only.
recipes.license: Work-for-hire contract; all IP transferred to commissioning party; terms vary by studio
recipes.commercial_notes: Work-for-hire contracts transfer full IP ownership of captured motion data to the commissioning party — unlimited commercial use, no redistribution limits, no revenue caps. Actual terms depend on the specific studio contract; ensure the contract explicitly states IP transfer and grants unlimited commercial use including game distribution, porting, and sequel rights. Cost range: $1,000–$10,000+ per day depending on studio, market, and session complexity. Performer SAG-AFTRA considerations may apply for union talent in the US.
